_comment_yield_average_horizon_turns: The forward-projection horizon (in turns) for a source's steady realized yield. SourceYield.realized is the AVERAGE food/turn the source delivers over the next N turns, computed by simulating the herd/patch forward N turns from its current state under the assignment's policy + worker count (the smooth policy rate, no kill-credit bank). A pure function of state, so the assign-time seed and the resolved row are identical (exact forecast==actual). Larger = a herd settled at its floor reads flat ≈ the regrowth there, and a projection under a LOWER floor sees the herd's decline within the window. Its OWN lever, NOT the expedition forecast_horizon_turns (a raid-length horizon). PLAYTEST DIAL. Validated > 0.
_comment_arrivals_horizon_turns: The forward-projection horizon (in turns) for a source's ARRIVAL SCHEDULE. SourceYield.arrivals[i] is the food landing i+1 turns from now, from the SAME forward simulation the realized average runs, but reported per TURN instead of averaged — so it answers 'on which turns does the food actually arrive', not 'how much per turn on average'. A big-game hunt at a high floor is genuinely lumpy (zeros between hauls); a forage patch or fast game lands something every turn. Kept SEPARATE from yield_average_horizon_turns (40) deliberately: this is a display span (how far ahead the larder chart plans), that one is a smoothing window. PLAYTEST DIAL. Validated > 0.

forage._comment_capacity_by_biome: THE HUMAN FOOD WEB, BY BIOME — the exact mirror of fauna_config.json's graze.capacity_by_biome (the ANIMAL food web), and the other half of the two-stock split (docs/plan_grazing_foundation.md §1). Human-edible biomass (seeds, nuts, tubers, fruit, shellfish, inshore fish) a tile of each biome carries at capacity; every FoodModuleTag tile is seeded a patch at its biome's value, and a biome reading 0 carries NO PATCH AT ALL. A DATA TABLE OVER THE 38 BIOMES, NOT A FORMULA: every biome must appear (validate() rejects a partial table — a missing row would silently read as an invisible zero-forage dead zone; ZERO MUST BE STATED). Per-BIOME, not per-FoodModule, deliberately: the two tables must be directly comparable tile-for-tile and must be able to DISAGREE WITHIN a module — that disagreement is the agropastoral decision. The FoodModuleTag model is untouched; the module still says what KIND of gathering a tile offers (and its seasonal_weight), this table says HOW MUCH is there. THE HEADLINE INVERSIONS, against the graze table: MixedWoodland 190 forage vs 55 graze (nuts, mast, berries under a canopy that shades out the ground cover — the flagship case); Floodplain/RiverDelta/AlluvialPlain 195-210 forage vs 130-140 graze (silt + water = CROPLAND, the farm, not the pasture); PrairieSteppe 70 forage vs 240 graze (grass: the animals feast, the humans get seed heads). Retired: the old flat carrying_capacity of 120 on every food-module tile, which made one food web spatial and the other a constant and so made 'your best farm is not your best pasture' UNTRUE BY CONSTRUCTION.
forage._comment_per_worker_biomass_capacity: THE NO-EQUIPMENT BASELINE, NOT THE EQUIPPED RATE - THE NUMBER MOVED, THE KEY DID NOT. This was 8.0, the BASKETED gather rate, for as long as the basket's only home for its own payload was an `unequipped` line in equipment.json. Quality tiers ended that: what the MATERIAL buys sits on the item's TIER, so the baskets' `flint` tier now declares `forage_carry equipped 8.0` and THIS key is what a bare-handed gatherer carries - 1.6, the value the item used to declare. Its ROLE changed and its name did not, deliberately: every caller passes it into EquipmentConfig::forage_per_worker_biomass_capacity, whose argument is the fallback either way, so a rename would churn ~40 call sites to say the same thing. WHAT MUST NOT HAPPEN is a readout quoting THIS number as 'what a gatherer collects': a surface with no band to resolve a tier against wants EquipmentConfig::equipped_reference(ForageCarry), which answers 8.0 off the item table. See .claude/rules/core_sim/equipment.md.
forage._comment_cultivation_moved_dials: The plant rung-2 BUILD dials (progress_per_turn, decay_per_turn and the old cultivating_yield_fraction) live in intensification_ladder.json -> the plant:tended rung's `build` block, and as of slice 4 so do the earned-knowledge dials (the old knowledge_progress_per_turn 0.05 / knowledge_completion_threshold 1.0 -> the ladder's `knowledge` block, previously duplicated verbatim in fauna_config's husbandry; the rate has since split into `learn_rate` 1.0 plus a per-knowledge `lesson_costs` entry of 20, which is the same 0.05). Both food webs climb — and now LEARN — on the same numbers. What remains here is the plant web's own economy.
forage._comment_cultivation: THE PLANT LADDER'S PAYOFFS — what each completed rung buys you. The BUILD dials (how long each rung takes, its feral decay, its investment dip) live in intensification_ladder.json; only the payoffs are here, exactly as fauna_config keeps pastoral_gain/pen_gain beside the ladder's build block. THE LAND OWNS K AND NO RUNG MAY LOWER IT (issue #433, docs/plan_flora_roster.md §4.3) — a retired concentration term shrank capacity and threw the remainder away, which made a commitment COST production, and that direction is now a config rejection. A rung MAY raise it: rung 3 does, through field_capacity_gain. Rungs 1-2 do not, so across those two what a rung changes is only WHICH PLANTS the constant production is made of — and every yield rate (food, fodder, trade) is the share-weighted average of the patch's effective basket, at every rung including wild. THE TWO RUNGS PAY IN DIFFERENT CURRENCIES, AND THAT ASYMMETRY IS THE MODEL (slice 7): RUNG 2 (tended) IS STILL A WILD STAND, better cared for — but since Flora Roster S2 a NEUTRAL one: its patch regrows at the WILD rate (tended_regrowth_gain 1.0), and you gather it under the full escapement-floor dial, drawing it down and able to over-farm it, exactly as a wild patch. What tending buys is WEEDING (tended_weeding_gain, see _comment_weeding) plus CONVERSION: tended_conversion_gain multiplies the FAVORED species' WHOLE YIELD VECTOR — food, fodder and trade alike, no role branch — and NOTHING ELSE in the basket, because tending is knowing YOUR crop and the volunteers standing beside it are still wild. A blanket multiplier on the whole basket would make every commitment pay ~gain regardless of what you favored, which erases the crop choice; on the favored term it COMPOUNDS with weeding, so favoring a dominant plant pays and favoring a marginal one barely moves. RUNG 3 (field) IS YOURS — you control its reproduction, so the basket is 100% the crop. WHAT IT DOES NOT CHANGE IS THE DRAW: a Field is gathered through the SAME forage_take path as a tended patch and a wild stand — escapement floor live, worker-capped, DRAWN DOWN — so it CAN be over-farmed and the overdraw warning fires on it. Strip a field every turn and it fails. PRODUCTION AND DRAW ARE SEPARATE CONCERNS: A RUNG MAY CHANGE PRODUCTION, NO RUNG CHANGES THE DRAW. What rung 3 buys instead is TWO PRODUCTION GAINS: field_capacity_gain (a sown field is planted densely with the competitors pulled out, so it HOLDS more standing crop) and field_regrowth_gain (you sowed it and you replant it, so it comes back faster). THIS IS THE ANIMAL WEB'S SHAPE, which is the argument for it — a herd already gets a regrowth multiplier and a density multiplier on the land's capacity at pastoral and again at pen; plants were the odd web out. Rung 3 does NOT take the tended conversion gain. RETIRED: tended_provisions_per_biomass 0.01, which made rung 2 a managed rate a full rung EARLIER than the animal side; and field_provisions_per_biomass 0.02, the rung-3 managed rate itself — A FIELD CHANGED HOW YOU HARVEST WHEN ITS JOB IS TO CHANGE HOW MUCH THE TILE GROWS, which made the harvest floor (the one pressure lever the player holds) do NOTHING at rung 3 and left the rung's payout unable to interpolate, being a different KIND of harvest from the rung below it. S2 RETIRED THE REGROWTH BOOST (tended_regrowth_gain 2.0 -> 1.0, NEUTRAL) on the grounds that competitor-removal was already explicit, and left rung 2's payoff owing; tended_conversion_gain (2.0) is what pays that debt — the term that makes a 25-turn Cultivate recoup in the teens of turns rather than the eighties. The regrowth lever stays (1.0 = neutral, a playtest dial if a small boost is wanted back). VALIDATED: field_regrowth_gain x field_capacity_gain > tended_regrowth_gain (tended < field, still monotone). Both rungs are drawn down through the same MSY skim now, and sustainable yield rides on r x K / 4, so every other term — the basket, the conversion, the tile's K, the shared r/4 curve — is common to both sides and cancels: the check is scale-free in the biome AND free of which species it is asked about, which is stronger than the retired form managed. Both field gains are also bounded at >= 1.0: a rung may RAISE K and may NEVER LOWER IT (issue #433), and a capacity gain below 1 is the retired concentration term that made a commitment cost production. tended_regrowth_gain likewise only forbids the INCOHERENT case gain < 1.0 (tending making a stand grow SLOWER than wild). THE TWO FIELD GAINS MULTIPLY through r x K / 4, and THE PRODUCT IS WHAT WAS HELD: they were chosen so the measured Field yield on the reference basket lands where the retired managed rate put it (core_sim/tests/field_reference_basket.rs). THE SPLIT BETWEEN THEM IS PROVISIONAL and a feel decision — they start near even. Move either and the other must move to hold the product. PLAYTEST DIALS.
forage._comment_weeding: THE LAND OWNS K, AND NO RUNG BELOW 4 RAISES IT **OR LOWERS IT** (issue #433, docs/plan_flora_roster.md §4.3). Committing a patch to one named plant (Cultivate/Sow, flora_config.json) does not change how much the tile produces — it changes WHAT THAT PRODUCTION IS MADE OF. TENDED (rung 2) WEEDS: the favored species' share rises to min(1.0, share x tended_weeding_gain) and the increase is taken from the LEAST ABUNDANT REMAINING SPECIES FIRST (ties by species key ascending), so the smallest weeds go first and the basket still sums to 1. FIELD (rung 3) PLANTS: the favored share is forced to 1.0 and every other to 0 — you sowed it, there are no volunteers. LEAST ABUNDANT FIRST IS DELIBERATE AND IS NOT 'LOWEST-YIELDING': ranking the weeds by yield would mean comparing a food rate against a trade rate, an exchange rate this codebase does not have and should not invent, and hay_grass (0 food, 0 trade, 0.2 fodder) has no non-arbitrary rank at all. Abundance is currency-free, deterministic from the composition alone, and independent of which crop was favored. WHAT THIS REPLACED: a CONCENTRATION term that multiplied the tile's K by min(1, share x gain) and DISCARDED the remainder, so committing a patch to a marginal plant CUT its production — the bug #433 fixed. effective_forage_capacity / patch_concentration / concentration_for_share and the field_concentration_gain dial (2.5) are retired with it; a Field forces the share to 1.0, so there is no gain left to tune. The cap at 1.0 is the model, not a safety rail: a basket is a whole, weeding can only move share WITHIN it, which is why rung 2's payoff has to come from tended_conversion_gain compounding with a bigger share rather than from the share alone. Validated finite and >= 1.0: below 1 a rung would weed AGAINST the crop it just committed to. PLAYTEST DIAL.
forage._comment_sow_share_cost: A SOW IS PRICED BY HOW MUCH OF THE TILE IT HAS TO REPLACE (docs/plan_standing_upkeep.md §4.15). The plant:field rung's build cost is its declared work_cost times clamp((1 - crop_share) / (1 - field_reference_crop_share), field_share_cost_floor, field_share_cost_ceiling), where crop_share is the chosen crop's share of the mix the Field is replacing — the WEEDED basket the rung below leaves behind, read the moment the Field LEG starts and held for the whole of that leg. Sowing a crop that already holds most of the ground is tidying; sowing one that holds a tenth is replacing the tile, and that is now a cost the player can see and choose against. IT IS AN ANCHORED RATIO, NOT A PENALTY, for capacity_per_tender's reason one entry down: field_reference_crop_share 0.5625 is THE REFERENCE BASKET'S OWN WEEDED SHARE (wild_emmer holds 0.375 of AlluvialPlain's realized basket — core_sim/tests/field_reference_basket.rs — and a Cultivate weeds it to 0.375 x tended_weeding_gain 1.5), so the shipped 75-work-unit price is PROVABLY PACING-NEUTRAL THERE and moving the anchor retunes the whole curve without touching the rung. A bare penalty would make 75 the cheapest case and inflate the entire plant branch; a bare discount would deflate it. BOTH CLAMPS ARE LOAD-BEARING. Without the floor, a tile already wholly the crop is FREE to sow — and you still lay the rows, still put the seed in, and still collect field_capacity_gain and field_regrowth_gain for it; 0.25 is 18.75 work units, about six turns at this rung's reference crew of three. Without the ceiling a marginal crop's price is bounded only by the anchor, which is a dial and not a promise; 2.0 is 150 work units, about fifty turns, and binds below a crop share of roughly an eighth. WHAT IT DOES NOT TOUCH: plant:tended's build cost (clearing wild ground is clearing wild ground — Cultivate is deliberately unchanged) and plant:field's UPKEEP, which is scaled_by source_load and reads the TILE's K, because holding a field is about how big the place is and never about what used to grow there. Two scale terms on one bill is the failure _comment_capacity_per_tender records. PLAYTEST DIALS — §4.14 owns the numbers.
forage._comment_capacity_per_tender: HOW MUCH STANDING CROP ONE TENDER CAN LOOK AFTER — the divisor that turns a TILE's own forage capacity (capacity_by_biome, via forage::tile_forage_capacity) into the TENDER-LOADS both plant rungs quote their upkeep.work_per_turn per (intensification_ladder.json -> plant:tended / plant:field, `scaled_by: source_load`). It is the PLANT TWIN of fauna_config.json's per-species animals_per_herder: the web owns the ratio, the rung owns the rate. IT IS DELIBERATELY ONE GLOBAL RATIO RATHER THAN ONE PER FLORA SPECIES. A patch's basket is SEVERAL species at once and a Field forces it to ONE, so a per-crop ratio would make the divisor SWING AS THE SOURCE CLIMBS THE LADDER — the same compounding the tile-K rule exists to prevent (the measure reads the TILE's K, never the patch's boosted carrying_capacity, because the patch's has already been multiplied by field_capacity_gain on the very ladder position the demand interpolates on, and billing both would land a Field near 10x a tended patch). 195.0 IS THE REFERENCE TILE'S OWN K (AlluvialPlain in capacity_by_biome), which is what makes the conversion PROVABLY PACING-NEUTRAL THERE: a tended patch on the reference tile goes on owing exactly 2.0 work/turn and a Field exactly 4.0, the rates the ladder already declared. Thin ground pays less (PrairieSteppe K 70 -> 0.718 / 1.436) and rich ground more (RiverDelta K 210 -> 2.154 / 4.308). A PLAYTEST DIAL — the number moves in docs/plan_standing_upkeep.md section 4.14.
forage._comment_field_conversion_gain: THE FIELD'S CONVERSION GAIN — the multiplier on the favored crop's whole yield vector once the patch is a SOWN FIELD, the rung-3 twin of tended_conversion_gain. IT EXISTS BECAUSE RUNG 3 HAD NO CONVERSION GAIN AT ALL. forage::favored_conversion_gain returned the tended gain at plant:tended and the IDENTITY at every other rung, Field included, so a Field converted each unit of biomass at HALF what the tended patch beneath it did. Reported from play: a completed tended patch paid 2.00 food/turn and the same tile sown to a Field paid 1.33, at the same two tenders — a rung paying LESS than the rung it was built on. Rung 3 was designed with its own rate (field_provisions_per_biomass); that dial was retired with the managed-harvest model (docs/plan_standing_upkeep.md section 4.10) and nothing replaced it. The Field's compensating payoffs — field_capacity_gain 2.53 and field_regrowth_gain 2.53 — only pay if you can CARRY more, and a fixed crew is carry-capped, so at that staffing the player paid 75 work units to swap a x2 conversion for gains they could not collect. IT SHIPS EQUAL TO THE TENDED RUNG'S AT 2.0, AND THAT IS DELIBERATELY THE MINIMUM: equality is exactly what restores the invariant and nothing more, and anything above it is TUNING, which section 4.14 owns. It reads as A FIELD KEEPS WHAT TENDING TAUGHT YOU — the crop knowledge does not evaporate when you sow it. VALIDATED finite and >= tended_conversion_gain, which makes the rule — A RUNG MAY NEVER PAY LESS PER UNIT THAN THE RUNG BENEATH IT — a load-time rejection rather than a number someone has to remember; the failure it guards is silent, because the Field's capacity and regrowth gains still read like a better rung right up until you count the food. A PLAYTEST DIAL.
forage._comment_navigable_river: The capacity_by_biome NavigableRiver row (130) is VESTIGIAL — a navigable hex now reads its UNDERLYING biome (resource_terrain) plus navigable_river_forage_bonus, so the row is bypassed. Left only to keep the table total.

hunt._comment_per_worker_biomass_capacity: THE NO-EQUIPMENT BASELINE, NOT THE EQUIPPED RATE - THE NUMBER MOVED, THE KEY DID NOT. This was 40.0, the SLEDDED haul rate, for as long as the sled's only home for its own payload was an `unequipped` line in equipment.json. Quality tiers ended that: the sled's `flint` tier now declares `hunt_carry equipped 40.0` and THIS key is what a sledless party drags - 12.0, the value the item used to declare. Its ROLE changed and its name did not, deliberately: every caller passes it into EquipmentConfig::hunt_per_worker_biomass_capacity (or ::pen_per_worker_biomass_capacity), whose argument is the fallback either way. WHAT MUST NOT HAPPEN is a readout quoting THIS number as 'what a hunter hauls': a herd row, a patch row or a Field's managed collection cap has no band to resolve a tier against and wants EquipmentConfig::equipped_reference(HuntCarry), which answers 40.0 off the item table. A PEN STILL SHARES THE HUNT HAUL'S RATE - `pen_carry`'s equipped side is resolved off the sled's tier through EquipmentStat::shares_equipped_rate_with, so that number still has exactly one home. See .claude/rules/core_sim/equipment.md.
